eu91_book:
Rofsky's book in Euro — readable object.

Interactive: "This is the book that Rofsky wrote about the
future of mankind." Provides intellectual context for
Rofsky's character and his predictions about the comet.
eu91_crate:
Crate object in Euro — interactable or obstacle.

Environmental object in the Euro streets. May contain
a hidden item or serve as a pushable obstacle.
eu91_intro:
Euro arrival narration and scene change (scene $91).

Guarded by $A5: set -> the actor dies at spawn. Otherwise it locks the player ($CFFC), hides the player actor, spawns the narration actors, plays 'We crossed the desert and finally arrived in the village of Euro.', sets $A5 and queues scene $96 (the guest room). $A5 is also read by three Watermia actors as the sign that the party has been to Euro.
eu91_men1:
Male townspeople group 1 in Euro — town introduction.

Multi-NPC (~134 lines). "This is Euro. It's a crowded merchant
town." Various male NPCs providing exposition about Euro's
mercantile culture and the Rolek Company's influence.
eu91_men2:
Male townspeople group 2 in Euro — Jackal warning.

NPC: "The other day, a man called the Jackal was asking
questions. He had the face of a killer." Warning about
the mysterious Jackal antagonist lurking in Euro.
eu91_merchant:
Street merchant in Euro — directs and warns the player.

Extended NPC (~203 lines). "Hey! Don't ever go over there.
Cross over to the other side!" Multi-phase merchant who
initially blocks passage, then opens up dialog about
Euro's commerce and dangers.
eu91_merchant_counter:
Merchant counter NPC in Euro — sells food.

Extended NPC (~120 lines). "How about a sweet apple?"
Operates a street stall with purchase dialog and
inventory management for food items.
eu91_peeking_man:
Peeking man in Euro — hides between buildings.

Animated NPC that peeks out from behind a building.
No direct dialog. Suspicious character adding to Euro's
atmosphere of hidden activity.
eu91_shop_door:
Shop door in Euro — access point to interior.

Interactive door that transitions to a shop interior.
Standard door mechanic with flag-based open/close state.
eu91_shop_queue:
Shop queue system in Euro (~386 lines).

Complex NPC queue management: "You can buy the best goods
in this shop." Simulates a line of customers waiting.
Player must wait their turn. Manages NPC positions,
turn order, and customer dialog. One of the more
elaborate town mechanics.
eu91_women1:
Female townspeople group 1 in Euro — mentions Rofsky and Erasquez.

Multi-NPC (~106 lines). "This is where the world-famous
Rofsky and the violinist Erasquez live." Establishes
Euro's cultural figures and their significance.
eu91_women2:
Female townspeople group 2 in Euro — back alley warning.

NPC: "There are many back alleys between the houses in town."
Hints at hidden areas and the labyrinthine Euro streets.
eu92_erasquez:
Erasquez in the Euro geezer house (scene $92): the Teapot test and the hint that sets flag $9F.

Solid and interactable. The interact handler tests the inventory first (BranchIfHasItem #19). With the Teapot (item $19) he prints 'Erasquez: I feel the presence of evil from somewhere in town...' and changes nothing (the item stays, $9F is not touched). Without the Teapot and $9F clear he sets $9F and prints 'Hey, you! I feel a strange power coming from you...' ending with 'At the right time, go to Mt.Kress and take a look at the Teapot.' and 'Rofsky marked Mt.Kress on Will's map!'. Without the Teapot and $9F set he prints 'The spirits' tears in the teapot reflect your true form.'. $9F is read by the Euro world-map exit (scene $91), which then stages menu $10 (Quit / Mt.Temple / Watermia) instead of menu $0F; flag $AC takes precedence with menu $1A.
eu92_rofsky:
Rofsky in the Euro geezer house (scene $92): first-visit argument, then teapot talk.

Flag $9E clear: at spawn the actor sets $9E, locks the player ($CFFC), plays the argument with Erasquez ('True genius is a violent thing!' / 'You just dash off packs of lies!!') and unlocks. Afterwards he stands solid; with the Teapot (item $19) he says 'Oh, that's the Teapot... It really does exist...', otherwise 'There is a dispute about the teapot enshrined at Mt.Kress temple...'.
eu93_found:
Man in the Euro power house (scene $93): a one-time strength gift.

$A6 clear: the actor sets $A6, prints 'You found it here. I understand your wishes. I'll give you the power at once.' and adds 1 to playerStr ($0ADE). $A6 set: 'Well, go.'.
eu94_employee:
Rolek Company employee — dismissive of children.

NPC: "What?!! A child... The old guys are talking about work.
Go over there!" Guards the business conversation. Overheard:
"I hear if I do business with this company..." — hints at
Rolek's commercial dealings.
eu95_ann:
Ann at the Rolek mansion (scene $95): the Jackal warning and the apple errand.

$D6 clear: she tells about the cloaked man asking for Kara and asks 'Should I tell Kara about it?' with the rows 'If you must!' and 'No, please don't!'. Row 1 prints 'I don't like that Kara. She acts like some kind of princess...' and sets nothing; row 2 or cancel prints 'Heh heh. I've found a weakness. Aah. I want an apple. Let's go to the marketplace!' and sets $D6.

$D6 set: with $E5 set she says 'I'll take care of Kara...'. Otherwise, without a Red Apple (item $28) she repeats the apple text; with an apple the first one sets $E3, the second $E4 (each removes the apple and prints 'Thanks. I can't eat any more.'), and the third removes the apple, prints the jewel text, gives item $01 and sets $E5 (a full inventory jumps to HiddenRedJewelInventoryFull and leaves $E5 clear, with the apple already spent).
eu95_neil:
Neil at the Rolek mansion (scene $95): two states by flag $A8.

$AA set: Neil dies at spawn. Otherwise he stands solid and his interact handler depends on $A8. $A8 clear (the Teapot has not been used here): 'To live for yourself or for others, that's the question...'. $A8 set: the handler prints the long dialog ('I finally realize how important my parents are to me. I wish I could have told them...'), sets $AA and queues scene $96.
eu95_neils_father:
Neil's father at the Rolek mansion (scene $95): a Moon Tribe reveal triggered by the Teapot.

$A8 set: the actor dies at spawn. Otherwise it stands solid with 'You can't go wrong by taking over the Rolek Company.' and waits for $A8 (set by UseItem_Teapot when the Teapot is used in tiles (28,09)-(2D,0D) of this scene). Then it locks the player ($EFFC, joypadMaskStd reads $EFF0), waits 4 ticks (WaitByte #03), starts music #1B, waits (WaitByte #3B), clears its solidity, walks, prints 'Moon Tribe: Ku ku ku... Soon this world will be wrapped in darkness. The previous owner of this body is now a skeleton sleeping under the shrine...', walks toward (0268,0060), starts music #04, waits 120 ticks (WaitByte #77), unlocks the player and falls through into code_07E21A (COP Die). Neil's mother runs the same walk and dies earlier in the same visit.
eu95_neils_mother:
Neil's mother at the Rolek mansion (scene $95).

$A8 set: the actor dies at spawn. Otherwise it stands solid with 'We've made money and wish to spend our remaining years enjoying life. Why don't you succeed us...' and waits for $A8 (the Teapot use); then it clears its solidity, walks off, moves toward (0268,0060), the same target as Neil's father, and dies when the walk ends (the actor definition falls through into code_07E314, COP Die).
eu96_erik:
Erik in the Euro guest room (scene $96).

$AC set: Erik dies at spawn. $AA set: 'I just don't understand women.'. Otherwise: 'I'm scared! What if I have to go to the bathroom and I can't find it?'.
eu96_kara:
Kara in the Euro guest room (scene $96): evening comment, morning reaction, departure.

$AC set: Kara dies at spawn. $AB set: her handler says 'To the west of here are the ruins of Ankor Wat. That is where the laborer's home is located. Let's go!', stores the companion slots $0D60-$0D66, stages the world-map move and queues scene $AC. Otherwise her handler says 'What a big house! The townspeople seem to be richer than the King...'; the main script waits for $AA, then for scratch $01 (set by Neil), moves and clears $01.
eu96_neil:
Neil in the Euro guest room (scene $96): the evening greeting and the morning scene.

$AC set: Neil dies at spawn. $AB set: he stands at tile (0A,0A) with the handler 'Neil: Take care, everyone.'. $AA set (Neil talked to the party in the mansion): the morning scene: locks the player ($EFFC), prints 'The next morning. Disappointment awaits...' and Neil's 'Good morning. Sorry about yesterday...' about taking over the company, starts music #1B, prints 'Kara, someone's come asking about you. Something about being an old friend.', sets scratch $01 and waits for it to be clear (Kara moves and clears it), then 'Hey! Come on in!' and spawns Hamlet (code_07DECB, which sets scratch $02); Neil waits for $02, starts music #02, prints Kara's reunion with Hamlet, sets $AB and unlocks. $A4 set: he dies at spawn. Otherwise the first greeting: sets $A4, locks the player ($CFFC), 'Well, make yourself at home.. I want to talk to my parents. It's been three years.'.
eu97_clerk1:
Shop clerk 1 in the Euro flea market — farewell dialog.

NPC: "Going home? Thank you very much." Friendly shopkeeper
who acknowledges the player leaving the store.
eu97_clerk2:
Shop clerk 2 in the Euro flea market — recognizes Neil.

NPC: "Aren't you Neil, from this village?! Rolek manages
this store." Connects Neil to his family's Rolek Company
and his hometown of Euro.
eu97_dark_medicine:
Dark Medicine in the Euro flea market (scene $97): a free one-time Dark Friar power gift.

$F1 set: the actor dies at spawn. Otherwise it asks 'That's called Dark Medicine. Try some?' (rows Yes/No). Yes: if $0B1C is 2 it prints 'The Dark Friar's power is strong enough!' and changes nothing; otherwise it writes $0B1C := 1, sets $F1 and prints 'Freedan's Dark Power has increased! The Dark Friar's power is increased!'. The text reports an increase; the code writes 1 even when $0B1C already holds 1.
eu97_life_medicine:
Life Medicine in the Euro flea market (scene $97): a free one-time max HP gift.

$F0 set: the interact handler prints 'I'm sorry... One to a customer.'. Otherwise it asks 'This is Life Medicine. Try some?' (rows Yes/No); Yes sets $F0, adds 1 to playerMaxHp and playerHp, prints 'Your power is increased!' and the actor dies. No money is taken.
eu9A_friezer:
Friezer in his Euro house (scene $9A).

$A7 set (the Mt. Kress entrance intro has played): the actor dies at spawn. Otherwise: 'I am the explorer, Friezer. I, too, plan on leaving my name in history as the discoverer of the Tower of Babel.'.
eu9A_max:
Max, Friezer's companion (scene $9A).

$A7 set: the actor dies at spawn. Otherwise it is solid and says "Max: I wonder where you're taking us exploring this time... I'm afraid it's up to the whims of the captain. Heh heh.".
eu9A_rudy:
Rudy, Friezer's companion (scene $9A).

$A7 set: the actor dies at spawn. Otherwise: 'The ruins are a great place. They just take my breath away.'.
eu9D_altar:
Altar of the Euro dark chapel (scene $9D): a hidden passage behind the statue.

Invisible actor with one polling loop and an interact handler. The loop first tests scratch $01; if it is clear it sets scratch $00 while the player stands in tiles (0F,07)-(10,09) and clears it outside (the player's idle code reads scratch $00 to pick the alternate sprite set). The handler prints 'What? The wind is blowing from behind the statue... Look?' with rows Yes/No; both rows clear the dialog box and Yes also sets scratch $01. On its next pass the loop plays sound $0101, applies BgChange #69 (the passage), removes the interact handler, clears $01 and continues. No persistent flag records the opening.
eu9D_bones:
Bones decoration in the Euro dark chapel.

Non-interactive prop in the chapel. Visual atmosphere
element suggesting the chapel's dark history.
eu9D_slaves:
Slave NPCs in the Euro dark chapel — disease exposition.

NPC: "Near our homes, various diseases are increasing...
Terrible diseases..." Connects Euro's dark chapel to the
broader themes of comet-related illness affecting the world.
euro_bg_scroll_actor:
Background scroll controller for Euro town.

Technical actor that manages parallax background scrolling
in the Euro town map. Provides the visual depth effect.
fireplace_journal:
Hidden journal in the fireplace at Lance's father's house.

Interactive object: "There's a journal in a crack in the
fireplace." Reveals backstory about Lance's father's
expedition — key lore item connecting to Will's father Olman.
gw82_necklace_stone:
Necklace stone drop — Lance's necklace piece on the Great Wall.

Collectible event item. Dialog: "A small stone falls." Then:
"Ha! This is part of the necklace Lance made for Lilly."
Key plot item that connects to Lance's story and his
relationship with Lilly.
gw82_trail_intro:
Will's monologue entering the Great Wall — following Lance.

Narration: "I followed Lance's trail to the Great Wall.
A corridor stretches..." Sets the scene for the Great Wall
dungeon chapter. Plays once on first entry with flag check.
gw83_lily:
Lilly at the Great Wall dive entrance — cutscene when Will reaches the ledge.

Dies at spawn when flag $93 is set. Otherwise it watches for the player in tiles (3B,08)-(3D,0B). On entry it enters display-filter mode (displayModeFlags $0080), sets $93, locks the joypad ($EFFC), prints "Wait!", walks Lilly in (sprite loops #33) and then toward the player, prints "Are you looking for Lance? I'll go with you!" and her closing line, restores the joypad and display mode and dies. The actor sets no party or escort state; the only persistent effect is flag $93.
gw83_switch:
Plug mechanism at the Great Wall dive entrance, released by a hit switch.

Dies at spawn when flag word $0152 is set. Otherwise it waits on WaitOnFlagByte ( #01, #01 ), the scratch flag raised by the hit_switch placed on the same tile (35,1B). It then shows frame #29 of spriteset_pickups_effects, clears $10 bit $2000, moves toward pixel ($0278,$0190) (StageMove ( #29, #04, #FF ), TickMove), spawns a debris burst, applies BG change #52 and sets $0152. The scratch flag is not cleared.
gw85_long_switch_spear:
Switch spear on the Great Wall rampway driven by scratch flag $03.

Solid frame #1F, WaitOnFlagByte ( #03, #01 ) for the hit_switch at tile (37,2C), ClearFlagByte of the same flag, retract frame #20, WaitByte ( #77 ), then back to solid. The retract time equals the other rampway actors; the script differs only in flag and frames.
gw85_multi_switch_spear:
Switch spear on the Great Wall rampway driven by scratch flag $04; two placements share it.

Solid frame #1D, WaitOnFlagByte ( #04, #01 ) for the hit_switch at tile (64,1D), ClearFlagByte of the same flag, retract frame #1E, WaitByte ( #77 ), then back to solid. The two placements at tiles (64,19) and (65,19) wait on the same flag and each clears it after leaving the wait, so the spear that is polled first consumes the trigger; whether the second one also retracts depends on the actor update order (not traced).
gw85_retractable_gate:
Retractable gate on the Great Wall rampway (scene $85).

Solid gate at frame #1D (MarkSolidHere and MarkSolidOffset ( #00, #03 )). It waits on WaitOnFlagByte ( #01, #01 ), the scratch flag raised by the hit_switch at tile (18,1A), and clears the flag (one-shot trigger). It then clears its solid tiles, shows the retract frame #1E with $10 bit $0100 set during the animation, waits 120 ticks (WaitByte #77) and closes again, so every later hit re-opens it.
gw85_short_switch_spear:
Switch spear on the Great Wall rampway driven by scratch flag $02.

Same script as the retractable gate: solid frame #1D, WaitOnFlagByte ( #02, #01 ) for the hit_switch placements at tiles (3B,29) and (29,2B), ClearFlagByte of the same flag, retract frame #1E, WaitByte ( #77 ), then back to solid. The retract time is the same #77 ticks as in the other three rampway actors; the names "short" and "long" only distinguish the switch flag.
gw85_spin_dash_gate:
Spin Dash gate on the Great Wall rampway (scene $85).

The actor loops on SetEntryHere and tests BranchIfPlayerAt ( #$0458, #$00D0 ). When that test matches, code_07E90F decides from the player's state: characterForm nonzero (Freedan or Shadow) passes, Will passes when abilityBitmask bit 2 ($0004, Spin Dash) is set, and Will without Spin Dash gets $03C0 written to the player actor's field $14 (the X position word), 152 below the X operand $0458 of the test. The code does not test an attack or a hit on the gate.
gw88_tomb_dark_space:
Dark Space portal in the Great Wall tomb area.

Hidden Dark Space access point in the tomb section.
Checks visibility/flag conditions before spawning the
Dark Space portal. Provides a save/heal point mid-dungeon.
gw8B_lance_lily:
Lance and Lilly reunion inside the Great Wall (~180 lines).

Major story scene. Lilly scolds Lance: "You're crazy! I've
been worried sick! What if you'd been..." Lance: "Oh.
That stone..." Will: "If you follow the stone..." Multi-phase
cutscene with character movement, dialog exchanges, and the
necklace subplot resolution.
mtA0_intro:
Mountain Temple entrance narration — describes Mt. Kress.

Story text: "There's a strange place at the summit of
Mt. Kress. There are mushrooms many times bigger than
a person." Establishes the oversized mushroom theme
of the Mountain Temple dungeon.
mtA2_mushroom_drop_gate:
Mushroom Drop gate of the Kress crossroads (scene $A2).

Dies at spawn when flag word $0159 is set. Otherwise it waits on WaitOnFlagByte ( #01, #01 ), the scratch flag that UseItem_MushroomWater raises when Will pours the item on the stem in tiles (14,08)-(16,09). It then locks the joypad ($EFFC), removes item #1A (Mushroom Drop) and plays sound #0F on channel 1 before each of the six BG changes #54-#59, sets $0159 and unlocks the joypad.
mtA5_mushroom_drop_gate_a:
Mushroom Drop gate A of the Kress circuit (scene $A5).

Dies at spawn when flag word $015F is set. Otherwise it waits on WaitOnFlagByte ( #01, #01 ), raised by UseItem_MushroomWater at stem A (tiles (2E,12)-(30,13)). It then locks the joypad, removes item #1A and plays sound #0F on channel 1 before each of the six BG changes #5A-#5F, sets $015F, unlocks the joypad and dies.
mtA5_mushroom_drop_gate_b:
Mushroom Drop gate B of the Kress circuit (scene $A5).

Dies at spawn when flag word $0167 is set. Otherwise it waits on WaitOnFlagByte ( #02, #01 ), raised by UseItem_MushroomWater at stem B (tiles (28,24)-(2A,25)). It then locks the joypad, removes item #1A and plays sound #0F on channel 1 before each BG change of the sequence #60, #61, #61, #62-#67, sets $0167, unlocks the joypad and dies.
wa78_centipede_man:
Centipede man NPC in Watermia — mentions the Sand Fanger.

Says: "I heard that a huge centipede called a Sand Fanger
lives in the Great Wall." Foreshadows the Great Wall boss.
wa78_children:
Children NPCs in Watermia — snake bite remedies.

NPC: "If you're bitten by a snake, you should run around like
crazy..." Humorous child wisdom about snake encounters.
Multi-child dialog with different advice.
wa78_crazy_man:
Crazy old man in Watermia — talks about the Tower of Babel.

NPC: "A crazy old man came here two years ago. He just talked
on about the Tower of Babel." Reference to someone who may
have returned from the Babel expedition.
wa78_diary:
Kara's diary in Watermia — optional secret read.

Interactive object with choice: "Kara's diary is secret.
Read it? Yes/No" — player can choose to read Kara's
private thoughts. Character development item.
wa78_flower:
Decorative flower in Watermia — ambient visual.

Non-interactable animated flower sprite for town decoration.
wa78_full_pad:
Full lily pad in Watermia — static platform.

Non-interactive lily pad decoration on the water surface.
Visual element of Watermia's water-town aesthetic.
wa78_glass_game:
Russian Glass mini-game controller in Watermia (~625 lines).

The most dangerous game in Watermia: "On full moon nights
they play Russian Glass." Complex mini-game with glass
selection, poisoned glass mechanics, NPC reactions, and
win/lose outcomes. One of the longest non-combat scripts.
wa78_intro:
Watermia arrival narration — town introduction.

Narration (~92 lines): "We went to the Water City, Watermia.
A beautiful town..." Multi-phase arrival cutscene with
party positioning and first impressions dialog.
wa78_kruk:
Kruk bird in Watermia — ambient animal.

Decorative NPC. Says: "Kyaah!! kyaah!!" — the Kruk call.
Animated animal for town atmosphere. Referenced by several
NPCs discussing Kruks as pets.
wa78_lance_camera_pan:
Camera-bob controller of the Watermia scenes ($78 and $7F).

At spawn the actor sets bit $1000 in its flags, writes cameraBoundsY = $0400 and waits for flag $8D (WaitOnFlagByte ( #8D, #01 ), set by wa78_intro in the middle of the arrival cutscene; in scene $7F the flag is already set, so the loop starts at once). It then reads camera_keyframe_078238 in a loop: every entry is a signed per-frame step and a duration; the step is added to cameraTargetY on every frame for that many frames, and an entry with duration 0 restarts the table. No dialog and no other actor is involved; the loop never ends while the scene runs.
wa78_lily_pad:
Moving lily pad in Watermia — small decorative platform.

Non-interactive floating pad on the water surface.
Visual decoration for the canal areas.
wa78_men:
Male NPCs in Watermia — extensive town exposition.

Multi-NPC group (~175 lines). "This is Watermia. The houses
are built on rafts. We like to move around." Various male
townspeople providing information about Watermia's culture,
raft-house lifestyle, and the Russian Glass tradition.
wa78_moving_pad:
Moving lily pad platform in Watermia — rideable water transport.

Complex movement actor (~336 lines). A large lily pad that
the player can stand on and ride across the water canals.
Handles player attachment, path following, and automatic
return cycles. Core navigation mechanic for Watermia.
wa78_moving_woman:
Wandering woman of Watermia (scene $78, spawn parameter #01).

The actor walks with NpcRandomWanderAI. Her interact handler has two texts chosen by flag $96 (the festival night, set by the Great Wall reunion and cleared when the Russian Glass game ends): with $96 clear she says 'This is Watermia. The houses are built on rafts. We like to move around.'; with $96 set she says 'A woman in pink chanted over that lotus leaf.'.
wa78_prize_kruk:
Prize Kruk of the Russian Glass game (scene $78, four placements).

The actor dies at spawn when $94 is set (the party has left for Euro) or when $97 is clear (the game is not won yet). In between it is a solid Kruk that waits while off screen, shows sprite frame #1C and says "These are the Kruks I was given. I have to let everyone know.".
wa78_water_kid:
Water-drinking child in Watermia — daily life dialog.

NPC: "We drink this water, cook with it, wash with it."
Shows how central water is to Watermia's daily life.
wa78_women:
Female NPCs in Watermia — water philosophy.

Multi-NPC group (~97 lines). "Water never stays in the same
place. It's always moving and cleansing." Women provide
philosophical commentary on water as a metaphor for life.
wa79_erik:
Erik in Luke's house (scene $79): three states by persistent flags.

$94 set: Erik dies at spawn. $97 set: 'I wish Lance and Lilly were coming, too...'. $96 set: 'There is a full moon tonight. The village seems different.'. Otherwise: 'Heh heh. I've found something good. Go outside and look behind the house. I feel a little guilty, but ...'.
wa79_kara:
Kara in Luke's house (scene $79): the largest party script, five states.

$94 set: Kara dies at spawn. $97 set: 'Neil's family runs a trading company in Euro.'. $96 set: 'A Kruk is an odd animal.'. Otherwise she stands solid and, with $91 clear, waits for scratch $02 (set by Lily) in the birthday sequence, spawns the cake child, prints the cake dialog and sets scratch $03; before that her handler says 'Watermia is very pretty, but I've heard a terrible rumor.'.

With $91 set (after the Lance and Lily scene $7F) she hands Will Lance's Letter (item $16): when $92 is clear she gives the item (on a full inventory she takes a Red Jewel, counted into jewelsCollected, or a Herb first), sets $92, locks the player ($CFFC) and prints Will's recollection ('So in the morning... When I awoke, Lance had disappeared...'). With $92 set her handler says 'What happened to Lance and Lilly? I'm worried.'. When the player holds neither a Red Jewel nor a Herb the branch falls through into the Red Jewel exchange (RemoveItem #01 and +1 on jewelsCollected) without a check.
wa79_lance:
Lance in Luke's house (scene $79): the party proposal and the later gifts.

With $97 clear and $96 clear: if $91 is set, or $90 is clear (he has not met his father yet), Lance dies at spawn. With $90 set and $91 clear he locks the player ($CFFC), moves the player's Y by -2, prints "Let's have Lilly's birthday party while we're all together.", sets scratch $01 (Lily's cue), waits for scratch $03 (set by Kara), prints "Ah, Lilly. Can I talk to you for a minute? I'll wait outside.", walks and sets scratch $04.

With $97 clear and $96 set he stands at tile (07,09) with "I made my father very happy before. I think he will slowly recover.".

With $97 set the handler depends on $A5: clear -> 'I'm sorry, but I want to stay here...' and scratch $01 is set (it releases Neil's departure talk); set -> the Red Jewel gift once: with $E2 clear it prints 'My father's getting better every day...' and gives item $01 (a full inventory jumps to HiddenRedJewelInventoryFull and $E2 stays clear), then sets $E2; with $E2 set it prints 'I hope you get to see your father soon.'.
wa79_lily:
Lilly in Luke's house (scene $79): the birthday surprise and four later states.

$97 set: she stands at tile (08,09); with $A5 clear she says 'I decided to stay in this town, too. Ask Lance the reason why.', with $A5 set 'Rumor is we're going to collide with a big star. I don't believe rumors like that.'. $96 set: tile (08,09), 'I hope Lance's father recovers quickly.'. $91 set: she dies at spawn (she is in the scene $7F exchange or gone). Otherwise she stands solid with 'I heard that Lance saw someone he knew in town.' until Lance sets scratch $01; then she animates, prints the surprise dialog ('What? Everybody remembered my birthday?'), sets scratch $02, waits for scratch $04 (set by Lance), says 'Excuse me everyone. I'll be right back..', walks off and queues scene $7F.
wa79_neil:
Neil in Luke's house (scene $79): four states by persistent flags, then the departure for Euro.

$94 set: Neil dies at spawn (the party has left). Otherwise he stands solid and the handler depends on $97 and $96. Before the glass night ($96 and $97 clear): 'The house on this raft gives me an idea for a new invention.'. $96 set: 'If you go west of here, there's a huge desert. You can't cross it on foot without Kruks. How will I get a Kruk?'. $97 set (the game is won): with scratch $01 clear he says 'You got Kruks? ... I think we should go west, to Euro...'; scratch $01 is set by wa79_lance's post-game handler when $A5 is clear, so the player has to talk to Lance first and Neil afterwards within one visit. With $01 set the handler prints the departure text, sets $94, stores the companion slots $0D60-$0D66, stages the world-map move and queues scene $91.
wa7A_lance:
Lance in his father's house (scene $7A): the visit that sets flag $90.

$90 set: Lance dies at spawn. Otherwise he stands solid with the handler code_07AB6B, which sets scratch $02. The main script waits for scratch $02, locks the player ($EFFC), starts music #1B and prints 'Will, do you recognize this person?
